title: Water tank sensors across apartment complexes
summary: Turn readings from thousands of cheap sensors into alerts and usage reports people can trust.
context: Hebbal Homes is fitting tank level sensors in 900 complexes. Each sends a reading every minute, over poor connections. The sensors are cheap: some drift, some go silent, and some send nonsense. Managers want an alert before a tank runs dry, and committees want monthly usage to help argue with tanker suppliers.
A false alarm at 2 am makes a manager stop trusting the system. A missed one means a whole building without water.
must_handle: A reading may arrive hours late, or twice.
A silent sensor is reported as silent, and never as an empty tank.
A faulty reading does not raise an alarm or spoil the monthly figure.
Monthly usage can be recalculated when a sensor turns out to have drifted.
Old minute-level data gets cheaper, while reports stay available.
show_in_answer: The path of a reading to an alert and to a report.
How the alert rule avoids false alarms, and how a missing sensor is treated.
How data is rolled up and kept over time.
